last_outcome: M1-03 done (iteration 17): 130 real, curated cities (id, name, admin1, country code, lat/lon, population) in apps/mobile/src/data/cities.json, the single source of truth for both a client-side pure search index (city-search.ts, exact/prefix/substring ranking with a population tie-break, diacritic-insensitive) and a generated seed migration (0009_seed_cities.sql via scripts/generate-cities-seed.mjs, drift-checked by tests/cities-seed.test.ts against the JSON, mirroring M1-02's build:engine pattern). A real GeoNames extract wasn't fetchable (no network access in this container) so a hand-curated real subset stands in; swapping it in later touches only cities.json. LoftPicker.tsx is a searchable picker screen using new plain-English strings.ts variants (loftPicker*, per PRODUCT.md 5's consent-boundary exception) and calling an injected LoftPickerDeps.saveLoft(city) contract rather than a real Supabase write, since no Supabase client exists in the mobile app yet (Q-002) -- filed M1-11 to close that gap. Two pre-existing PGlite tests (loft-snap.test.ts, visibility.test.ts) assumed an empty/small cities table for their own controlled fixtures; both now `delete from cities` first to isolate themselves from the new real seed data. /code-review --effort high found two real issues, both fixed: handleSelect had no protection against out-of-order async saves (a slow first tap's save could resolve after a faster second tap and silently move the displayed checkmark back to the stale city) -- fixed with a latestSelectionId ref gating both the .then and .catch; city-search.ts's matchRank compared raw lower-cased strings with no diacritic stripping, so typing the ASCII form of an accented dataset name (Sao Paulo, Zurich, Bogota, ...) found nothing -- fixed by NFD-normalizing and stripping combining marks on both sides of the comparison. gate:tests floor raised 138 -> 157 (+19).
